results.name: Paella Valenciana (Casa Carmela)
results.why_it_is_special: Traditional wood‑fire paella using orange wood, chicken, rabbit, beans and saffron; a family‑run institution preserving Valencia’s iconic rice dish.

results.name: All i Pebre (Bon Aire Restaurante)
results.why_it_is_special: Classic eel stew seasoned with garlic, paprika and potatoes; a signature dish of the Albufera region that reflects local fishing heritage.

results.name: Horchata & Fartons (Horchatería Daniel)
results.locality_or_neighbourhood: Avenida de la Horchata, central Valencia
results.why_it_is_special: Iconic chufa‑based horchata served with freshly baked fartons; a beloved Valencian tradition celebrated since 1949.

results.name: Horchata & Fartons (Horchatería Alboraya)
results.why_it_is_special: 100 % Chufa Denominación de Origen Valencia, artisanal preparation; the go‑to spot for authentic horchata and fartons.

results.name: Fideuà (Mercat Central)
results.why_it_is_special: Seafood noodle dish cooked with fresh local seafood; a staple of Valencian cuisine available at stalls inside the historic market.

results.name: Buñuelos de Calabaza (Horchatería Daniel)
results.why_it_is_special: Pumpkin‑flavoured fritters, a traditional sweet treat that showcases Valencia’s festive pastry heritage.

results.name: Paella (Restaurante El Palmar)
results.why_it_is_special: Offers a range of paellas, including seafood and traditional versions, in a setting surrounded by rice fields and the Albufera lagoon.
